messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected in us-east-1 — streaming stalls and SLO breaches. Auto-created incident 3759123456. Severity: SEV2. Please paged oncall and join bridge.
alice.chen: I'm seeing p95 jump from ~2.1s -> ~3.8s, p99 from ~5s -> ~22s. Streaming sessions aborting, retries increasing 3x.
bob.martin: Cache telemetry shows prefix-cache miss rate jumped to ~92% right after the prefix-hash:v3 rollout (~10:18 UTC). Lots of 404s on prefix keys.
carol.sre: Confirmed high eviction and miss churn on kv-buckets. Looks like salt/namespace change mapped keys differently. Tagging @deploy-bot — can we roll back?
deploy-bot: Deploy record: prefix-hash:v3 deployed at 2026-09-14T10:18Z. Rollback available: `deploy rollback prefix-hash:v3`.
dave.eng: Canary health failing for streaming nodepool. Two options: rollback the hash OR enable backward-compat mode so old keys resolve while we rehash.
alice.chen: Customer impact: support ticket count x8, some commercial customers reporting repeated stalls at 10:25z. Priya please prepare customer comms.
priya.product: On it. Drafting brief: "We're investigating increased latency and streaming interruptions affecting a subset of requests. Mitigations in progress." Will post update once we have ETA.
carlos-custops: Noted — highest-usage customer sees recurring stalls and is asking for ETA. Need timeline ASAP.
bob.martin: Immediate mitigation - enable runtime compat shim to accept old prefixes + start background rehash. Commands:
```
rbx config set runtime.prefix_cache_compat true --env=prod --scope=region:us-east-1
rbx jobs start rehash-prefixes --source=old-hash --target=prefix-hash:v3 --concurrency=4
```
carol.sre: Also kicking off hot-prefix warming from traces to reduce miss storm and bumping prefetch batch from 1 -> 3: `rbx cache warm --top=5000`.
dave.eng: I'll open a small hotfix to flip compat + prefetch. If that doesn't hit <10% miss in 5m, we rollback. Which should we prefer? alice?
alice.chen: Ops decision: compat-mode first (less blast radius). Monitor for 5m. If miss rate >10% after 5m, rollback to v2.
incident-bot: Bridge opened: https://zoom/bridge/3759123456 — invited: @alice.chen @bob.martin @carol.sre @dave.eng @priya.product. Handoff to oncall @carol.sre in 15m if unresolved.
deploy-bot: Rolling config change to us-east-1 (30 hosts). Status: 6/30 succeeded, rolling.
bob.martin: After first rollout batch: miss rate down to ~62%, p99 improved from ~22s -> ~12s. Still above SLO but trending good.
priya.product: Sent initial notice to affected customers. Will update after stabilization.
carlos-custops: Customers acknowledged and asked to be notified when p99 back under SLO.
alice.chen: Plan B (rollback) prepped. Rollback steps in runbook and expected 3-5 minute impact window. Bob/Dave to execute if needed.
bob.martin: Rollback snippet in runbook:
```
# quick rollback
deploy rollback prefix-hash:v3 --grace=30s
# then monitor: rbxtools obs query --metric=cache_miss_rate --window=5m
```
carol.sre: Compat-mode rollout finished at 10:38Z: 30/30 hosts. Current metrics: miss rate ~18%, p95 ~1.9s, p99 ~3.6s. Streaming stalls largely cleared. :thumbsup:
alice.chen: Nice. Customer impact reduced; handoff to post-incident actions: root-cause = prefix-hash migration lacked backward-compat shim + insufficient canary keyspace sampling. Need postmortem.
dave.eng: I'll open a postmortem PR with action items: stricter canary sampling, automatic warm-up after hash changes, add compatibility flag to migration playbook.
priya.product: Sending update to customers: "Mitigations applied; majority of impacted requests recovered. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Will paste final note to incident channel.
carol.sre: Handoff: next oncall for follow-up verification is @dave.eng in 30m. Bridge will stay open for 10m unless regression seen. Incident state -> mitigated (monitoring). :eyes:
incident-bot: Incident 3759123456 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. P95/P99 trending back under SLO. Please file postmortem with tag SEV2 and reference this thread.
